accepted.s: Agroforestry is best described as:
o: Growing trees together with crops and livestock on the same land
Growing crops only beneath naturally occurring forest canopies
Replacing agricultural land entirely with forest species
Growing only commercial tree plantations on degraded land
accepted.x: Agroforestry integrates trees, crops and livestock on the same land.
accepted.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a broad description of forestry.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated benefit of agroforestry?
o: Permanent elimination of all climate risks
accepted.x: Agroforestry diversifies farm income, conserves soil, improves fertility, stores carbon and enhances climate resilience, but it cannot permanently eliminate all climate risks.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme claim that goes beyond the stated benefits.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s: India became the first country to adopt a National Agroforestry Policy in:
accepted.x: India adopted the National Agroforestry Policy in February 2014 and was the first country to do so.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact month and year from nearby policy dates.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GROW report:
1. GROW stands for Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry.
2. It was associated with NITI Aayog.
3. It estimated that about 8.65% of India’s geographical area is under agroforestry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The GROW report by NITI Aayog uses the expansion ‘Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry’ and places the agroforestry area at about 8.65% of India’s geographical area.
accepted.tq: Check the expansion, institution and numerical estimate separately.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s: The Central Agroforestry Research Institute (ICAR-CAFRI) is located at:
accepted.x: ICAR-CAFRI is located at Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-location association.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s: The Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) is implemented under:
accepted.x: Agroforestry receives support through the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry under PM-RKVY.
accepted.tq: Separate the funding programme from related forestry schemes.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s:
With reference to Trees Outside Forests in India (TOFI), consider the following statements:
1. It is a programme of MoEFCC and USAID.
2. It was launched in 2023.
3. It was launched in seven States, including Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: TOFI is an MoEFCC-USAID programme launched in 2023 in seven States, one of which is Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Verify the partners, launch year and geographical coverage together.
accepted.sec: Agroforestry - National Agroforestry Policy 2014, GROW report, CAFRI, Trees Outside Forests

accepted.s: The Nagar Van Yojana is run by the:
accepted.x: The National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB) runs the Nagar Van Yojana.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct implementing body rather than the research institution.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: The Nagar Van Yojana targets, between 2020–21 and 2026–27:
accepted.x: The scheme targets 600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas during 2020–21 to 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Split the paired targets carefully; the figures are deliberately reversible.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the progress of the Nagar Van Yojana?
o: 600 projects were sanctioned in 28 States and 3 Union Territories at a cost of ₹458.53 crore.
400 projects were sanctioned in 28 States and 3 Union Territories at a cost of ₹654.30 crore.
620 projects were sanctioned in 28 States and 3 Union Territories at a cost of ₹654.30 crore.
620 projects were sanctioned in 3 States and 28 Union Territories at a cost of ₹654.30 crore.
accepted.x: The reported progress is 620 sanctioned projects in 28 States and 3 Union Territories, costing ₹654.30 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the project count, territorial coverage and total cost as one fact-unit.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: Under the Nagar Van Yojana, the first instalment released was:
accepted.x: The first instalment released was ₹458.53 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the instalment released from the total sanctioned cost.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign commenced on:
accepted.x: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign began on 5 June 2024.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact launch date of the named campaign.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Pradesh — Telangana Ku Haritha Haram
Telangana — Great Green Wall of AP
Andhra Pradesh — Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana
accepted.x: The Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana is associated with Chhattisgarh. Great Green Wall of AP, Namo Van-Nagar Van and School Nursery Scheme are listed for Andhra Pradesh, while Telangana has Telangana Ku Haritha Haram.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure State–scheme pair and eliminate swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events or programmes in chronological order:
A. Adoption of National Agroforestry Policy by India
B. Launch of Trees Outside Forests in India
C. Commencement of Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam
D. Beginning year of the Nagar Van Yojana target period
accepted.x: The relevant years are 2014 for the National Agroforestry Policy, 2020–21 for the Nagar Van Yojana target period, 2023 for TOFI and 2024 for Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest policy and latest campaign first, then place the middle events.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: Vanamahotsav is held in the:
accepted.x: Vanamahotsav is observed in the first week of July.
accepted.tq: Recall the observance period without confusing it with a monsoon-season launch date.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: Vanamahotsav was started by K. M. Munshi in:
accepted.x: K. M. Munshi started Vanamahotsav in 1950.
accepted.tq: Link the founder with the exact year rather than the general post-Independence period.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s:
The revised 2021–30 framework of the Green India Mission targets which of the following regions or ecosystems?
1. Aravallis
2. Western Ghats
3. Himalayas
4. Mangroves
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The revised framework targets the Aravallis, Western Ghats, Himalayas and mangroves.
accepted.tq: Check whether the list is complete before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Green India Mission:
1. It is one of the missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
2. It is implemented through Joint Forest Management Committees.
3. It is funded partly from National CAMPA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Green India Mission is one of the NAPCC missions, is implemented through JFMCs and receives partial funding from National CAMPA.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional status, implementation mechanism and funding source.
accepted.sec: Afforestation schemes - Nagar Van Yojana, NAEB, state schemes

accepted.s: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 established:
o: National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds
District-level funds without national or State funds
Only the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund
accepted.x: The Act established both National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds.
accepted.tq: Avoid the false exclusivity implied by ‘only’.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly characterises the National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds?
o: They are temporary departmental deposits without public-account status.
They are non-lapsable public accounts that earn interest.
They are non-lapsable public accounts that cannot earn interest.
They are lapsable private accounts that do not earn interest.
accepted.x: The funds are non-lapsable public accounts and earn interest.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between lapsable and non-lapsable accounts and between earning and not earning interest.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the two-tier CAMPA arrangement?
o: National CAMPA carries out field work while State CAMPAs frame national policy.
State CAMPAs set national policy and National CAMPA implements village-level works.
National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy, while State CAMPAs carry out the work.
Both National and State CAMPAs are headed by the State Forest Minister and perform identical functions.
accepted.x: National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy; State CAMPAs undertake implementation.
accepted.tq: Compare the policy-setting and implementation roles rather than the names alone.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: The prescribed distribution of CAMPA funds between State funds and the National fund is:
accepted.x: Ninety per cent is allocated to State funds and ten per cent to the National fund.
accepted.tq: Keep the direction of the split clear: the larger share goes to the States.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Before a project involving diversion of forest land starts, the agency diverting the land is required to pay:
o: Compensatory afforestation cost and the Net Present Value of the lost forest ecosystem
A wildlife management fee without compensatory afforestation cost
Only the cost of planting new trees
Only the Net Present Value of the lost ecosystem
accepted.x: The agency must pay for compensatory afforestation as well as the NPV of the lost forest ecosystem before the project begins.
accepted.tq: Apply the rule to the project-start condition and include both required components.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated use of CAMPA funds?
o: Financing unrestricted private urban housing projects
accepted.x: CAMPA funds may support regeneration, wildlife management, catchment treatment, relocation from protected areas, human-wildlife conflict management and forest-fire prevention. Unrestricted private urban housing is not a stated use.
accepted.tq: Identify the option outside the listed public forestry and wildlife purposes.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Progress in the utilisation and implementation of CAMPA funds is tracked through the:
accepted.x: The e-Green Watch portal is used to track CAMPA progress.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the monitoring portal from similarly named forestry programmes.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the reported status of CAMPA funds by 2024?
o: The fund held over ₹66,000 crore, but only about 30–35% was being used.
The fund held ₹654.30 crore, but only 10% was being used.
The fund held over ₹66,000 crore, of which about 90% was being used.
The fund held over ₹6,600 crore, of which about 30–35% was being used.
accepted.x: By 2024, CAMPA funds exceeded ₹66,000 crore, while only about 30–35% was reported to be in use.
accepted.tq: Separate the fund size from the utilisation percentage.
accepted.sec: CAMPA - CAF Act 2016, National and State CAMPA, NPV, fund uses

accepted.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, forest rights are recognised in favour of:
o: Only private companies holding forest diversion approvals
Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers
All persons residing in any urban area near a forest
accepted.x: The Act recognises forest rights of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
accepted.tq: Use the exact beneficiary category instead of a broad population description.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: The nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who handles this subject?’ institutional identification method.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly states the eligibility conditions under the Forest Rights Act?
1. Scheduled Tribes must have been living in and dependent on forests before 13 December 2005.
2. Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence for three generations.
3. Three generations in this context means 75 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. ST eligibility relates to residence and dependence before 13 December 2005, while OTFDs must establish residence for three generations, equivalent to 75 years.
accepted.tq: Check the date, category-specific condition and numerical meaning separately.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: Which of the following is an individual forest right recognised under the Forest Rights Act?
o: Ownership of all protected areas in a district
Automatic right to divert any forest land for industry
Self-cultivation and habitation up to four hectares
Exclusive control over all minor forest produce in the State
accepted.x: Individual rights include self-cultivation and habitation up to four hectares.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an individual entitlement from broader community or administrative powers.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s:
Which of the following is a community right under the Forest Rights Act?
1. Nistar
2. Grazing
3. Fishing
4. Ownership and disposal of minor forest produce
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Nistar, grazing, fishing, and ownership and disposal of minor forest produce are listed community rights.
accepted.tq: Test the completeness of a rights list instead of selecting only the most familiar items.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: For the purposes of community rights under the Forest Rights Act, bamboo is treated as:
o: A critical wildlife habitat resource only
accepted.x: Bamboo is included within minor forest produce under the listed community rights.
accepted.tq: Resolve the classification of a commonly confused forest product.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups and the right to protect, regenerate and manage Community Forest Resources are classified as:
o: Temporary rights available only during disasters
accepted.x: Habitat rights for PVTGs and Community Forest Resource rights are included among community rights.
accepted.tq: Separate individual rights from community rights using the classification table.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the process of determining forest rights under the Forest Rights Act?
o: District Level Committee, Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee
Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee
Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee, Gram Sabha
Gram Sabha, District Level Committee, Sub-Divisional Level Committee
accepted.x: The Gram Sabha initiates the process; claims then pass to the Sub-Divisional Level Committee and the District Level Committee.
accepted.tq: Follow the administrative sequence from the grassroots body upward.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: Diversion of forest land for public utilities such as schools and dispensaries may be recommended by the:
accepted.x: The Gram Sabha may recommend diversion of forest land for specified public utilities such as schools and dispensaries.
accepted.tq: Identify the grassroots authority associated with the decision.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Critical Wildlife Habitats from critical tiger habitats?
o: Critical Wildlife Habitats are notified under the Forest Rights Act, while critical tiger habitats under the Wildlife Protection Act require mandatory Gram Sabha consultation.
Critical Wildlife Habitats are notified by CAMPA, while critical tiger habitats are notified under the Forest Rights Act.
Both are notified only under the Wildlife Protection Act and require no Gram Sabha consultation.
Neither category has a statutory relationship with the Gram Sabha.
accepted.x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are notified under the Forest Rights Act. Critical tiger habitats under the Wildlife Protection Act require mandatory Gram Sabha consultation.
accepted.tq: Compare the legal basis and consultation requirement rather than treating the two habitat categories as identical.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: As of 2024, the reported number of claims received and titles distributed under the Forest Rights Act was approximately:
o: 42 lakh claims received and 52 lakh titles distributed
52 lakh claims received and 42 lakh titles distributed
52 lakh claims received and 30–35 lakh titles distributed
66 lakh claims received and 42 lakh titles distributed
accepted.x: By 2024, about 52 lakh claims had been received and 42 lakh titles distributed.
accepted.tq: Keep the sequence of the two figures—claims first and titles second—unchanged.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR

accepted.s: The right to fell and transport bamboo under the relevant legal framework is derived from the:
accepted.x: The right to fell and transport bamboo is associated with the Forest Rights Act, not merely with the Indian Forest Act amendment.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated legal instruments.
accepted.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006 - rights, eligibility, Gram Sabha, CWH, CFR
